app.keeps_overlaps_every_note_exactly_as:
Keeps overlaps.
Every note exactly as the shapes make it, all on one channel.
Notes on the same key can overlap or start on the same tick.
app.removes_overlaps_all_on_one_channel:
Removes overlaps, all on one channel.
Where two notes on the same key overlap, the earlier one is cut
where the later one starts, and the later one is stretched
to where the earlier one would have ended.
Notes starting on the same tick become one note: the loudest wins,
and it's as long as the longest of them.
app.a_channel_per_overlap_shapes_whose:
A channel per overlap.
Shapes whose notes overlap go on different channels, each on its own
track (channel 10 is skipped). Shapes that don't clash share a channel.
The box below picks what counts as an overlap.
app.split_same_key_at_the_same: Split: same key at the same time
app.split_any_notes_at_the_same: Split: any notes at the same time
app.same_key_shapes_only_get_split:
Same key: shapes only get split when they play the same key at the same time.
Any notes: shapes get split whenever their notes play at the same time,
even on different keys (e.g. two parallel lines, or lines starting on the
same tick). Shapes that follow one after another still share a channel.
snap.tip:
The grid points and notes snap to while you draw and drag (Shift = don't snap).
Note lengths: 1/4 = a quarter note (one beat), 3/8 = a dotted quarter, 1/6 = quarter-note triplets.
Custom… = any length you set up.
snap.kind_tip:
Empty = one plain note (16 = a 16th note), the left number isn't used.
/ = that many notes (3 / 16 = three 16th notes).
. = a dotted note (one and a half notes), .. = double dotted (one and three quarters).
snap.divided_by_tip: Splits the length into this many equal steps (3 = triplets).
app.history_tip: The History list: every change as a step; click one to go back to it.
app.every_tip_searchable_opens_at_the: Every tip, searchable. Opens at the tool you're using.
app.formula_tip: Drag a line like Linear: a pattern (Wave, Zigzag, Bounce or one you saved) swings the velocity up and down around it. Its settings show next to the tool buttons; changing them changes the line you just drew.
velocity_formula.pattern_tip: The pattern along the line. Your saved patterns (Formula ▸ Pattern along the line ▸ Custom…) are in the list too.
velocity_formula.loops_tip: How many times the pattern repeats between the line's two ends. Parts of a loop work too (4.5).
velocity_formula.number_tip: "{name}" in the pattern's formula, in velocity steps (a Wave of height 20 goes up to 20 above the line and 20 below it).
app.ctrl_flat_shift_snap_enter_done: Ctrl = flat · Shift = snap · Enter = done · select a shape to edit only its notes
app.a_ppq_of_or_more_many:
A PPQ of {PPQ_WARN} or more: many MIDI programs can't open the file.
Spiderweb still writes it.
app.128_the_standard_keys_0_127:
128: the standard keys 0–127, which every MIDI program reads.
256: keys 0–255, for players that support them (handy for tunings like 31edo).
Many MIDI programs can't read keys above 127, and playback here skips them.
app.where_copied_and_pasted_notes_start:
Where copied and pasted notes start:
First note at tick 0: the first note lands right on the cursor / play line.
From the bar line: the empty space from the bar line before the first note
comes along, so the notes keep their place in the bar.
app.ctrl_shift_v_the_notes_copied:
Ctrl+Shift+V: the notes copied in Domino (Ctrl+C there) become one shape here.
It starts at the play line, like pasting in Domino (see the start setting above).
Every track's notes go into the one shape; controllers and other events are left out.
Ticks are taken as they are: use the same PPQ here.
app.ctrl_shift_c_copies_the_selected:
Ctrl+Shift+C: copies the selected shapes' notes (all notes when nothing is selected).
In Domino, paste with Ctrl+V at the cursor, or double-click a bar line in a track.
Multi channel: each channel goes into its own track, from that one down.
Ticks are copied as they are: use the same PPQ there.

tumour_window.tilts_every_bump_its_two_f:

tumour_window.which_side_of_the_line_the: Which side of the line the bumps go (left / right as you go along the line from its start).
tumour_window.only_matters_where_the_lin:

tumour_window.only_this_part_of_the_line: Only this part of the line gets bumps (0 % = its start, 100 % = its end).
tumour_window.fit_the_bumps_evenly_the_d:

the range exactly, with the last one landing right on its end.

pattern_dialog.shape_help:
t goes from 0 to 1 while the shape is drawn. The drawing is fitted to the curve: if it ends where it started (like a circle), it's as wide as from the curve's start A to its end B; if not, it starts at A and ends at B. It follows the curve, so bending the dotted curve bends the shape.
Works: numbers, t, + - * / ^ ( ), pi, e, sin cos tan asin acos atan sqrt exp ln log abs min max floor.
pattern_dialog.shape_edited_by_hand: Edited by hand. Its start and end points stay where they are (their handles can move).
pattern_dialog.whole_shape: The whole shape, between the curve's ends A and B. Drag a point to change it by hand; double-click the line to add a point, right-click a point to remove it. Alt + drag: a sharp corner. Wheel = zoom, drag empty space = move.
pattern_dialog.title: Pattern along the line
pattern_dialog.name: Name
pattern_dialog.sym_tip: Symmetric halves: only the first half of the formula counts. The second half is made from it, mirrored (like an arch) or turned half way round (like an S).
pattern_dialog.edit_formula_tip: Type your own formula. Any name in it other than x (like height) gets its own number box.
pattern_dialog.help:
One loop: x goes from 0 at its start to 1 at its end; y is how far to the side of the curve, in keys (up on a curve going to the right).
Works: numbers, x, + - * / ^ ( ), pi, e, sin cos tan asin acos atan sqrt exp ln log abs min max floor.
pattern_dialog.help_polygon:
One loop: x goes from 0 at its start to 1 at its end; y is how far to the side (outward), in hundredths of the polygon's height. Every side gets the pattern, and it grows and shrinks with the polygon.
Works: numbers, x, + - * / ^ ( ), pi, e, sin cos tan asin acos atan sqrt exp ln log abs min max floor.
pattern_dialog.help_drawer:
One loop: x goes from 0 at its start to 1 at its end; y is how far to the side of the curve, in hundredths of the board (100 = the whole board). The drawing keeps these sizes when it's placed, so they grow and shrink with it.
Works: numbers, x, + - * / ^ ( ), pi, e, sin cos tan asin acos atan sqrt exp ln log abs min max floor.
pattern_dialog.fit_view_tip: Show all of it again. Mouse wheel = zoom in and out; drag empty space (or middle-drag) = move around.
pattern_dialog.back_to_formula_tip: Forget the changes made by hand: the loop follows the formula again.

pattern_dialog.only_saved: Only your saved patterns can be deleted (the grey ones come with Spiderweb).
pattern_dialog.edited_by_hand: Edited by hand: every loop along the line follows this one.
pattern_dialog.one_loop: One loop, as long as it is on the curve. Drag a point to change it by hand; double-click the line to add a point, right-click a point to remove it. Alt + drag: a sharp corner. Wheel = zoom, drag empty space = move.

help.about.title: About Spiderweb
help.about.tip: Version, license, and where Spiderweb keeps your files.
help.about.text: Free to use, share and change under the MIT License.
New versions, the source code and problem reports: {WEBSITE}

Spiderweb can look there for a new version by itself (set how often at the bottom of this page; Never turns it off). When there is one, a small window says what's new in it and has a button to open the download page. Nothing is downloaded by itself: to update, download the new Spiderweb.exe and put it in place of the old one. Your autosave and shapes stay.
All of the code was written by an AI model (Claude Opus 5.5, by Anthropic). Kanade Tachibana directed the project: decided what it should do, tested it and asked for changes.
Spiderweb's folder holds your autosave (and autosave-backup), your shape library (shapes), the MIDI files you generate (output) and errors.log, where the details go if something goes wrong.

help.welcome.title: Welcome to Spiderweb
help.welcome.tip: Draw lines and shapes on the piano roll and they become notes. Pick a tool at the top; a short tip like this one explains each the first time. F1 or the Help button: every tip, searchable.
help.welcome.text: Draw lines, curves and shapes on the piano roll; every key they cross gets notes, like drawing notes by hand but in one stroke.
1. Pick a tool at the top (Line, Polyline, Freehand, Curve, Arc, Custom shape, Funnel, Text) and draw.
2. Select a shape to change it: drag its points, or change its settings in the panel on the right.
3. Space plays it. Right-drag listens to the notes under the mouse.
4. Set PPQ, BPM and the output file under Project, then Generate MIDI.
Your work is saved on its own (autosave) and comes back next time. Save… keeps a copy as a project file.
The first time you use a tool or feature, a small tip explains it. You can turn tips off or show them all again in this Help window (bottom).
help.whats_new.title: What's new
help.whats_new.tip: What changed in each version, newest first.
help.whats_new.text: What changed in each version, newest first. This page opens by itself the first time a new version starts.
Version 1.3.0

• Update check: Spiderweb can look for a new version when it starts (every time, once a day, week or month, or never) and show what's new in it. Set it in Help → About; "Check now" looks right away. Nothing is downloaded by itself.
• This What's new page.

• Formulas: right-click a curve → Formula. "Shape of the curve" makes it a circle, spiral, flower, heart, figure 8, slow or fast start, or S-curve. "Pattern along the curve" lays a wave, zigzag or bounce along it. Custom… makes your own, with a preview you can zoom and move. Lines, arcs, drawer curves and funnel curves have them too. "Turn into plain curve" makes the result an ordinary curve.
• Velocity pane: a Formula tool (a line with a wave, zigzag, bounce or saved pattern swinging around it).
• Symmetric halves stay symmetric when a formula's shape is changed by hand or turned into a plain curve.
• Funnel: lines on both sides of the wall make two halves, each with its own notes running to the wall. Notes ending on the wall make the same steps as notes starting on it.
• Easier picking of lines, strokes, funnel parts and a box's corners and sides. Clicking the faint dashed line under a formula curve selects the shape.
• Steep lines give 1-tick notes to keys that share a tick.
• The Custom… formula window and the tumour graph have their own undo (Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y). The graph has From / to boxes and a right-click menu on its points.
• Curves fitted from drawn paths follow long, wiggly paths with fewer anchors, and sharp corners stay sharp.
Version 1.2.0
• Inside fill: Spam ends (round, keep, drop, no slivers, stretch), Normal / Outline, Overlaps cancel out, and outlines with gaps can be filled.
• Turn into live shape (Ctrl+L): lines, curves and arcs become one custom shape that can be filled.
• Tumours: their own window, Rotation and Slant, and graphs so the numbers can change along the line.
• Join (Ctrl+G) and Split (Ctrl+Shift+G), and Split here on a line's right-click menu.
• Snap: the usual list of note lengths with note pictures, plus Custom….
• History panel, Keys 128 / 256, picking shapes by their notes, Paste from Domino can start at the bar line, more tips, and typing anywhere in Help searches.
Version 1.1.0
• Copy to Domino (Ctrl+Shift+C) and Paste from Domino (Ctrl+Shift+V).
Version 1.0.0
• The first version.

help.select.title: Select (V)
help.select.tip: Click a shape to select it, drag it to move, drag its squares to reshape. Drag empty space = scroll, click empty space = move the play line. Double right-click = to the last drawing tool and back.
help.select.text: Click a shape (its line or one of its notes) to select it (where shapes overlap: a line first, then the one on top; a selected shape under the mouse stays the one you drag); Ctrl+click selects more (Ctrl+A = all). Drag a shape to move it (all selected ones move together), drag its squares to reshape it.
Drag empty space to scroll. Click empty space (no drag) to move the play line there.

Right-click a shape (or one of its notes) = its menu (delete, duplicate, copy, flip, turn, add a point...). Right-click empty space = deselect. Double right-click switches between Select and the last drawing tool.
Blue curve handles can be dragged with any tool.

help.line.title: Line (L)
help.line.tip: Drag from start to end, or click the start and then click the end.
help.line.text: Drag from the start to the end, or click the start and click the end (the line follows the mouse in between; right-click or Esc cancels).
Each key the line crosses gets one note, starting where the line reaches that key, so a slope becomes a smooth staircase. Points snap to the grid (Snap at the top); hold Shift to place them freely.
Last note (panel): the last note ends on the line's end, or starts exactly on it.
Right-click it: Formula (a shape or a pattern along it, see Formulas).
help.poly.title: Polyline (P)
help.poly.tip: Click point after point (or drag each piece). Double-click or right-click to finish.
help.poly.text: Click point after point, or drag each piece. Double-click, right-click or Enter finishes it; Esc cancels.
Selected polyline: drag its squares to move points; middle-click on it adds a point where it fits best.
Last note (panel) works at every point: each piece is its own line.
help.free.title: Freehand (F)
help.free.tip: Drag to draw. Straighten (panel) turns it into perfect lines, curves or shapes.
help.free.text: Hold the mouse button and draw.

Straighten (panel, 0-100) makes it perfect: 0 = as you drew it, higher = straighter lines and smoother curves. A stroke that ends where it started becomes a perfect circle, ellipse, square, rectangle or triangle. The higher, the simpler (a slightly oval loop becomes an ellipse, then a circle). The stroke as drawn is kept, so change it any time. New strokes use the last number you picked.
help.free.words: draw hand pencil smooth straighten shape recognition
help.curve.title: Curve (C)
help.curve.tip: Drag from start to end (or click both), then bend it with its blue handles. Middle-click the curve to add an anchor.
help.curve.text: Drag from the start to the end, or click both. Then shape it (see Curves: anchors and handles): drag the blue dots to bend it, middle-click the curve to add an anchor.
Right-click it: Formula (a shape like a spiral or heart, a pattern like a wave along it: see Formulas), Symmetric halves (one half follows the other), add an anchor, and the usual menu.
help.arc.title: Arc (A)
help.arc.tip: Click the start, a point it passes through, and the end. Or drag from start to end, then move the mouse to bend it and click.
help.arc.text: A piece of a perfect circle. Click its start, a point it passes through, then its end. Or drag from the start to the end, then move the mouse to bend it and click.
It's round as the piano roll looks while you draw it. Put the end on the start for a whole circle.
Selected: drag its round middle point (any tool) to bend it, its squares to move the ends. Right-click it: Formula (a shape or a pattern along it, see Formulas).
help.custom.title: Custom shape (S)
help.custom.tip: Pick a shape in the panel (or make one with Drawer…), then drag a box to place it.
help.custom.text: Pick a shape in the panel, or draw your own with Drawer…. Then drag a box on the piano roll (or click two corners); the drawing stretches to fill it. Ctrl keeps its drawn proportions.
Its inside can be filled (see Inside fill). Square, Circle and Triangle (Q / O / T) show next to Custom shape while it's picked: they make that shape straight away (Ctrl = perfect, as it looks).
A placed shape keeps its own copy: changing the library shape later doesn't change it.
help.box.title: Circle and Polygon (O / Q)
help.box.tip: Drag a box (or click two corners). Ctrl = a perfect circle or polygon as it looks. Polygon: pick the points and kind (polygon, star, crossing star) in the panel.
help.box.text: Drag a box on the piano roll, or click two corners. Ctrl makes it perfect as it looks on screen (a circle, a square, an equal-sided triangle or star).

Polygon: the panel sets how many Points it has (3 = triangle, 4 = square, 5 = pentagon…) and its Kind. Polygon has a flat side at the bottom. Star: outer and inner points take turns; Inner size is how far out the inner points are, in % of the outer ones (100 = a polygon with twice the points). Crossing star: joins every Skip-th point with straight lines that cross, like a pentagram (5 points, skip 2); when the two share a divisor it's several loops (6 points, skip 2 = two triangles). Change them any time with the polygon selected; the panel's numbers are also used for the next one you draw.

The sides can have a pattern: right-click the polygon → Formula → Pattern along the line (a wave, zigzag, spikes, your own…). Every side gets the same pattern: Each piece gives every side all the loops, Across all runs them on round the whole outline. Its height is in hundredths of the polygon's height, so it grows with the shape. Symmetric halves work on it too. "Turn into plain lines" makes the result plain lines (the polygon settings go).

They're custom shapes, so their inside can be filled (see Inside fill) and they resize, turn and skew like any custom shape (see Custom shapes: resize, turn, skew). With Live shape on they're drawn into the live shape instead.
help.box.words: rectangle ellipse oval shapes square triangle polygon pentagon hexagon star pentagram hexagram
help.funnel.title: Funnel (N)
help.funnel.tip: Draw its line, then its wall (drag, or click twice each). Then middle-click on the line to start a curve there.
help.funnel.text: Draw the funnel's line, then its wall (drag each, or click twice). Either can come first; a wall earlier in time than the line's start makes a reverse funnel. Ctrl while drawing or dragging the wall keeps it centred on the line.

Middle-click on the line (any tool) to start a curve there: curves go to both ends of the wall. Middle-click near a curve to add an anchor it goes through. The curves have anchors and handles (see Funnel curves).

With a funnel selected, a line drawn to (or from) its wall is added to it (two-line funnels). Lines on the other side of the wall make their own half, with its own notes running to the wall: they just start (or end) on the wall; the wall setting is for the first line's side.
Panel: the wall (notes end on it, or start on it), the inside (spam or long notes) and the gate. Tick "Different start and wall gate" to let the gate change from the start to the wall.
help.text.title: Text (X)
help.text.tip: Click on the piano roll and type. Esc = done. The letters become a custom shape.
help.text.text: Click on the piano roll and type (Enter = new line, Esc = done). The letters become a custom shape, so they can be filled, moved, resized, turned and skewed.
Panel: font, size (font size, or rows = how many keys capital letters are), weight and italic, plus:
Letter spacing: extra room between the letters, in 1/1000 of the font size. Minus numbers pull them closer together.
Line spacing: room between lines (Enter starts a new line), in % of the font's own line spacing.
Align: where the text sits on the spot you clicked. Left = it starts there, Centre = its middle is there, Right = it ends there. With several lines it also lines them up.
Text is a custom shape, so Empty, Fill, Spam and Outline spam work on its letters too (see Inside fill).
Threshold (Fill / Spam): how much of a key's height has to be inside a letter for that key to play there. 50% = the key's middle. Lower = chunkier letters, higher = thinner.
Grow: makes the letters' strokes thicker, in keys (minus = thinner). Big values can look odd in tight corners.
Click a text with the Text tool (or double-click it with Select) to retype it. Drag, Shift+arrows, double-click (a word) or Ctrl+A select letters; Ctrl+C / X / V copy, cut and paste them.
help.live.title: Live shape (G)
help.live.tip: Lines, curves, arcs, freehand and boxes you draw now go into ONE custom shape. Close its outline to fill it. Right-click empty space to start the next one.
help.live.text: With Live shape on, Line, Polyline, Freehand, Curve, Arc, Square, Circle and Triangle draw into one custom shape (the selected one, or a new one) instead of making separate shapes. Outlines that meet end to end join up, so a closed drawing can be filled (see Inside fill). Points snap onto the drawing's ends; clicking a polyline's first point closes it; letting go of a freehand stroke near its start closes it. Right-click empty space (deselect) to start the next shape.
While it's on, the selected shape's points show (purple squares): drag them with Select. Points in the same spot move together, and a point dropped on another one joins it.

Select tool: click a stroke of the selected shape to pick it: Del deletes it, a curve shows its handles, a freehand stroke can be straightened. Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V, Ctrl+H / Ctrl+J and Ctrl+Left / Ctrl+Right copy, paste, flip and turn just that stroke (Esc unpicks it: then they work on the whole shape again). A copied stroke is pasted into the selected custom shape, a grid step later and a key lower each time (nothing selected: into a new shape). Right-click a stroke = its menu, also: save the drawing to the shape library.
help.turn_live.title: Turn into live shape (Ctrl+L)
help.turn_live.tip: Select lines, curves, arcs (or custom shapes) and press Ctrl+L: they become one live shape, so they can be filled. Split into separate shapes (Ctrl+Shift+G) gives them back.
help.turn_live.text: Lines can't be filled, custom shapes can. Select one or more lines, polylines, freehand strokes, curves or arcs (custom shapes too) and press Ctrl+L, click Turn into live shape under the shape list, or right-click one → Turn into live shape. They become one live shape (a custom shape) with each of them as a stroke of its own kind: curves stay curves with their anchors, arcs stay arcs, a straightened freehand stroke stays straightened. Then Fill, Spam and Outline spam work (see Inside fill), and its strokes can be edited like any live shape's.

The notes stay the same, and so do the velocities (where shapes play at the same time, the first selected one's win). With Multi channel each stroke still remembers the shape it came from, so strokes that clash still get channels of their own; the shape list says how many channels a shape uses (orange above 15).
What changes (Spiderweb asks first when it applies): tumours become fixed points, and "Last note: starts on it" is dropped.

Going back: Split into separate shapes (Ctrl+Shift+G, or right-click → Split back into the old shapes) gives the old shapes back exactly as they were, tumours and all, as long as the drawing wasn't changed (moving the whole shape is fine; resizing, turning, flipping or editing its strokes isn't: then it splits into groups of touching strokes instead). Ctrl+Z always works.

help.fill.title: Inside fill (custom shapes)
help.fill.tip: Empty = just the outline. Fill = one long note per key inside. Spam = back-to-back notes of the gate. Outline spam = the outline chopped into notes of the gate. Ends = what to do with the bit that doesn't fit a whole gate. Outline (box next to Fill / Spam) = the edge on its own channel.
help.fill.text: How a custom shape (and text) is filled, in the panel:
Empty: just the outline, like lines (upright parts get 1-tick notes).
Fill: one note per stretch of each key inside.

Spam: back-to-back notes of the gate. Start: Auto = each key from its own left edge; Aligned = on the gate grid from the song's start (straight columns); Centred = what doesn't fit a whole gate is shared between both ends (peaks come out the same on both sides).

Ends: with a gate of 1 tick every key is filled exactly. With a longer gate, a key's stretch is rarely a whole number of gates, so something has to give at its ends: Ends picks what happens to the bit that doesn't fit a whole gate. The same goes for Outline spam. The pictures show the same triangle each time.
Round to a gate (new shapes start with this one): a whole gate if it's at least half a gate, else dropped. Every key gets at least one gate, so the edge stays in whole gates.
Keep leftovers: kept as a shorter note, so the edge follows the outline exactly.
Drop leftovers: dropped. A key too short for even one gate still gets one shorter note, so points end in thin slivers.
No slivers: like Drop leftovers, but no note shorter than a quarter gate.
Stretch gates: each key's gates are stretched or squeezed a little so a whole number fits exactly. Start doesn't matter then, so there's one picture.
Outline spam: the outline chopped into notes of the gate.

Gaps: where the outline isn't closed (red dots in the drawer), Fill and Spam close it with straight lines, shown dashed, and the buttons turn orange. Loose ends that nearly touch (within 1/64 beat and 1 key) are joined to each other first; every open part left is closed from its end back to its start. An open part that's almost straight (never more than half a key or 1/64 beat from that closing line) has nothing inside, so it isn't filled: it just keeps its notes. Close the gaps yourself to decide exactly where the edge goes.

Normal / Outline (the box next to Fill and Spam): Outline puts the notes along the edge of what's filled on a channel of their own (with Overlaps cancel out ticked that's every edge, around every filled bit; unticked, only the outer edge) and the inside's on another, with the same gate so they line up (where both would play, the outline's note is kept). It needs Channels: Multi channel; with the others it's all one channel and the box turns orange.

Overlaps cancel out (ticked unless you change it): where outlines overlap, the overlap stays empty, and a shape inside a shape makes a hole. Untick it to fill inside any outline, overlaps and holes too. (Text always fills its letters the way the font means them.)
Lines, curves and arcs can't be filled: turn them into a live shape first (Ctrl+L, see Turn into live shape).
Spiderweb asks before making more than a million notes.

help.custom_edit.title: Custom shapes: resize, turn, skew
help.custom_edit.tip: Drag a corner or side to resize, just outside a corner to turn, just outside a side's middle to skew. Drag inside to move it.
help.custom_edit.text: A selected custom shape (and text) shows a box. The mouse pointer changes to show what a drag will do.
Move: drag anywhere inside it (Select tool). It moves in grid steps; Shift = free.
Resize: drag a corner square. The opposite corner stays put; Ctrl keeps its proportions.
One side: drag a side (or its middle square) to move just that side.
Turn: drag from just outside a corner. It turns around its middle in 15° steps; Shift = any angle.
Skew: drag from just outside a side's middle. That side slides along itself in grid steps (Shift = free) while the opposite side stays.
Turning happens as the piano roll looks; zooming only one way afterwards slants it.
help.tumours.title: Tumours
help.tumours.tip: Bumps along the line: size, length, distance apart, rotation, which side. Length 0 = spikes (a zigzag). The … next to a number = a graph, so it changes along the line. Bumps take the current zoom's shape: zoom first, then set them up.
help.tumours.text: Select a line, polyline, freehand stroke, curve or arc, click Tumours… in the panel (or right-click it: Tumours…) and tick Tumours in the window that opens: bumps along it. The window can stay open; it shows whatever you select. The line's points stay draggable; the line as drawn shows faint and dashed.
Shape: triangle, square, circle or parabola.
Size: how far the bumps stick out, in keys.
Length: how long each bump is along the line, in ticks. 0 = spikes (a zigzag).
Distance: from the start of one bump to the start of the next, in ticks.

Rotation: tilts every bump while its two feet stay on the line. Plus leans it forward (the way the line runs), minus leans it back; 90 lays it flat along the line, 180 turns it over to the other side.
Slant (square bumps only): 0 = a square, 100 = the top narrows to a point, minus = the top is wider than the bottom.

Graphs: the … button next to Size, Length, Distance, Rotation or Slant opens a graph of that number along the whole line (from its start on the left to its end on the right). 100 % = the number in the box, so the box still scales the whole graph. Drag the points (Shift = free), click to add one, or pick a preset or type a formula. Right-click a point: Value… types its exact place along the line and its value (in %, or as the number it makes), Delete point removes it (not when only two are left; deleting an end makes the next point the new end). Show picks how high the graph is shown, or type your own From / to. Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y undo and redo the graph's changes while the window is open. The part outside the tumour Range is greyed out. A number following a graph says "× graph" in blue; Flat (off) removes it. The piano roll shows the change as you go; OK keeps it, Cancel (or Esc) puts the graph back as it was.
Side: alternating, left, right or random.

Straight or Bent with the line: this only matters where the line curves under a bump (long bumps on a curve, arc or circle). Straight builds each bump on a straight shortcut from where it starts to where it ends, so it looks angular. Bent with the line makes it follow the curve underneath, so the whole thing stays round. On a straight line both look the same.
Lead in: the bumps grow from nothing over that many ticks from each end, so the line eases into them.
Range: only part of the line gets bumps. Fit: a whole number of bumps fits exactly (seamless on a full circle).

The zoom matters: bumps are shaped as they look on screen when you change a tumour setting (a circle comes out round at that zoom). Zooming afterwards stretches them like the rest of the piano roll; changing any tumour setting again reshapes them for the zoom you're at now. So zoom to how you want to see them first, then set them up.

help.claw.title: Claw machine (beta)
help.claw.tip: Changes the selected shapes' notes: cuts slices of time out, or keeps some notes and trashes some. The shape stays as drawn, so you can move it or open the claw again to change it. Accept keeps it, X puts the notes back.
help.claw.text: Beta: the claw machine is new and may still change in later versions.
The mouse wheel over a dropdown (Mode, Period, Trash every) picks the next or previous choice.

Select one or more shapes, then right-click one: Claw machine… (or press Ctrl+K). The notes change on the piano roll while you try settings. Accept keeps the change (one Ctrl+Z takes it back); X or Esc puts the notes back as they were. Reset sets everything back to the start, where the claw changes nothing.

You can keep working in the main window while it's open. It follows the selection: select other shapes to work on them. When you select other shapes or change something in the main window, the claw tried so far is kept (as its own Ctrl+Z step).

The claw is kept with the shape: the outline stays as you drew it, and moving, resizing or reshaping it makes new notes that go through the same claw. Open the window again to change it, or Reset + Accept to take it off.
Mode By time works like the claw machine found in other piano rolls:
Period: the claw works on this much time at a time, over and over, starting at the shape's first note.

Trash every: each period is cut into equal slices and one is thrown away. 1/4 = the first quarter, 2/4 = the second quarter, and so on. Notes in that slice go, notes crossing its edges are cut there, and all later notes move earlier to close the gap, so the notes end sooner.

Time dist: bends time inside each period. Turned right: long notes first, then faster and faster (a bouncing ball, a drum roll before a drop). Turned left: the other way round. Drag it up / down (Shift = fine), use the mouse wheel or the arrow keys; it stops at 0 for a moment on the way past. Hold the right mouse button on it to point it at the mouse. Middle-click (press the mouse wheel) puts it back to 0. It works even with Trash every at (none).
Stretch to compensate: stretches everything back to the shape's full length, so the notes get longer instead of ending sooner.
Remove short notes: removes the tiny pieces the claw leaves (under 1/24 beat). Notes that were that short already stay.

Count notes / Count keys / Count chords: keep some, then trash some, over and over to the end. Notes are counted in time order; keys are counted up from the shape's lowest key (keys with no notes count too), so every other key makes stripes; a chord = all the notes starting at the same moment.
Random: keeps about that many notes in every hundred. New random picks other notes; the same shape always gets the same pick.
Shorten instead of remove (not in By time): the notes picked to go stay, only shorter: this much of their length.

help.straighten.title: Straighten (freehand)
help.straighten.tip: 0 = as drawn. Higher = straighter lines, smoother curves, perfect shapes.
help.straighten.text: Freehand strokes (and freehand strokes in a live shape: pick the stroke first) have a Straighten number in the panel, 0-100.

0 = exactly as drawn. Higher = the stroke may stray further from your drawing to become simpler: wobbly parts become straight lines and smooth curves, sharp turns stay corners. A stroke that ends where it started becomes a perfect shape: circle or ellipse, square or rectangle, triangle (or another straight-sided shape). Turning it up makes it simpler (an oval → a circle, a rectangle → a square); a loop keeps its kind and its tilt.
The drawing is kept underneath, so you can change the number any time. New freehand strokes use the last number you picked.

help.curves_pen.title: Curves: anchors and handles
help.curves_pen.tip: Drag a round anchor to move it, drag a handle dot to bend. Alt = sharp corner. Right-click an anchor to remove it.
help.curves_pen.text: Curves (the Curve tool, funnel curves, curve strokes in the drawer and in live shapes) work like a pen tool.

Handles: drag the dot at the end of a blue handle line to steer the curve (its direction) and set how strongly it pulls (its length). On a smooth anchor both handles turn together. Handles can be dragged with any tool.
Anchors: drag an anchor to move it; its handles come along. The curve's two ends are anchors too (the squares, Select tool).
Adding and removing: middle-click the curve to add an anchor there (then drag it like any other). Right-click an anchor to remove it, or a handle dot to pull it back in (a corner).
Corners: Alt+drag a handle = move only that one (a sharp corner). Alt+drag an anchor = pull new handles out of it.
help.curves_pen.words: bezier pen anchor handle bend corner
help.symmetric.title: Symmetric halves
help.symmetric.tip: Right-click a curve: one half follows the other, mirrored (an arch) or turned (an S).
help.symmetric.text: Right-click a curve → Symmetric halves: one half follows the other. The curve gets an odd number of anchors with the middle one on the line of symmetry; editing one half rewrites the other.
Mirrored (like an arch): the second half is the first one reflected.
Turned half way round (like an S): the second half is the first one turned around the middle.
Off: the halves go their own way again.
help.join.title: Join and split
help.join.tip: Select several lines, polylines, freehand strokes, curves or arcs, then press Ctrl+G (or Join shapes into one curve under the shape list, or right-click). Right-click any of them → Split here cuts it in two.
help.join.text: Join: select two or more lines, polylines, freehand strokes, curves or arcs, then press Ctrl+G or click Join shapes into one curve under the shape list (or right-click one of them → Join shapes into one curve). They become one Curve shape: ends that touch are joined (with a corner there), and the curve's anchors and handles can be edited like any curve. Freehand strokes are turned into a smooth curve that follows them closely.

Shapes that don't touch stay separate pieces of the same curve: nothing is drawn between them and they make no notes there, but they're selected, moved, flipped and copied together. Each piece works like a shape of its own (its own row of tumours, range, graphs and last note). The squares at a piece's ends can't be removed.

Tumours: each shape keeps its own tumours after joining (even when they're the same), so no bump moves. The first time you change any tumour setting of the joined curve, the whole curve gets the settings shown in the tumour window, and the bumps run on across the joints. So set up each shape's tumours first, then join. Each shape keeps its velocities (where shapes play at the same time, the first selected one's win); Last note comes from the first shape.

Split here: right-click a line, polyline, freehand stroke, curve or arc where you want to cut it → Split here. On an anchor or a polyline point it's cut there; anywhere else a point is added there first. An arc becomes two arcs of the same circle; a freehand stroke is cut at its nearest drawn point (a straightened one is cut from the straightened line, and the halves are no longer straightened, so they look the same). Each half keeps the velocities it had, and its tumours stay where they were: each half gets its part of the Range and graphs (Fit is turned off, keeping the distance it had worked out). Only a bump across the cut is cut off, random sides are picked again and Lead in starts again at the cut.

Split into separate shapes (Ctrl+Shift+G, under the shape list, or right-click): a joined curve goes back to one curve per piece (and per shape that kept its own tumours). A custom shape, like one drawn with Live shape, splits into one shape per group of strokes that touch each other. Each part keeps the velocities it had.
Notes: a joined curve plays like one curve, so where two lines meet it doesn't start a new note the way two separate lines would.

help.funnel_curves.title: Funnel curves
help.funnel_curves.tip: Middle-click the line: a new curve start. Middle-click near a curve: an anchor. Select tool: click a curve again to highlight it (Del, right-click = shapes, linking).
help.funnel_curves.text: Middle-click on a funnel's line (any tool) to start curves there (a diamond); middle-click near a curve to add an anchor. The curves work like any curve: drag the anchors and handle dots (see Curves: anchors and handles). A start's two curves are linked, so they change together (see Linking funnel curves).

Highlighting: with the funnel selected and the Select tool, click one of its lines or curves again to highlight it (purple). A curve comes with the curves linked to it (teal); Ctrl+click adds or removes just one.
Del = delete it. Right-click = Formula (shapes and patterns, see Formulas), Back to the default curve, and linking.
Ctrl+H / Ctrl+J = flip the curves (end to end / inside out). Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V = copy a curve's shape onto others. Esc = clear the highlight.
help.funnel_curves.words: curve start anchor link mirror formula highlight
help.funnel_links.title: Linking funnel curves
help.funnel_links.tip: Linked curves change together (Ctrl while dragging = only this one). To link: Select tool, click a curve, Ctrl+click another, right-click → Link curves.
help.funnel_links.text: Linked curves change together: drag an anchor or handle on one and the others follow, and adding or removing an anchor does it on all of them. A new curve start's two curves come linked as mirror images of each other, so the funnel stays even on both sides.

Changing just one: hold Ctrl while dragging (or middle-clicking to add an anchor). If that gives it a different number of anchors than the others, it stops following them until they match again or you link them anew.
Linking curves yourself (any curves of one funnel, also on different lines):
1. Select the funnel, then with the Select tool click one of its curves: it's highlighted (purple), with the curves already linked to it (teal).
2. Ctrl+click more curves to add them (Ctrl+click a highlighted one to leave it out).
3. Right-click the curve whose shape you want to keep → Link curves:
Auto: each curve takes whichever way is closer to how it looks now.
Mirrored / Same shape (the name depends on which way the curves open): the same curve, reflected across the line or the same way round.
Flipped: turned end to end, so what happens near the start on one happens near the wall on the other.
Unlink: the highlighted curves go their own way.
The right-clicked curve keeps its shape, the others are reshaped to follow it. A curve can only be in one link group: linking it again takes it out of its old group.
Ctrl while drawing or dragging the wall keeps it centred on the line, so mirrored curves stay exact mirrors on the piano roll.

help.formulas.title: Formulas: shapes and patterns
help.formulas.tip: Right-click a curve, line or arc ▸ Formula: give it a shape (Circle, Spiral, Heart…) or a pattern along it (Wave, Zigzag, Square wave, Spikes…). Drawer curves, funnel curves and polygon sides have it too.
help.formulas.text: Right-click a curve ▸ Formula (a Curve tool curve, a line, an arc, a curve stroke in the drawer, or highlighted funnel curves). It has two parts, and a curve can have both at once. (On a line or an arc it works the same way: below, "curve" means them too.)

Shape of the line: the line takes a shape. One that ends where it starts (Circle, Flower, Heart, Figure 8) is as wide as from the curve's start (A) to its end (B) and sits on that line; the others start at A and end at B. They're round as the piano roll looks when you pick them.

Pattern along the line: a pattern repeats along the line (along its shape, if it has one): Wave, Zigzag, Bounce, Square wave, Sawtooth, Teeth, Spikes, Half circles, Stair steps, Swell, Fading wave. Loops = how many times (4.5 works too). Its height is in keys.

Symmetric halves (in the Formula menu under each list, in the Custom… window and in the side panel): only the first half of the formula counts, and the second half is made from it: Mirrored (like an arch) or Turned half way round (like an S). A shape that ends where it starts stays closed. It works on your own formulas and saved ones too, and Save keeps it.

The curve you drew stays as a dashed line with its anchors and handles: bend it and the shape and pattern follow. The side panel shows the selected curve's numbers (like turns, petals, height and Loops). On a joined curve, Across all runs the loops on from piece to piece and Each piece gives every piece all of them. Separate curves each get their own pattern: join them first to run one pattern across them.

Custom… (at the top of each list) shows every shape or pattern with its formula and a box for each of its numbers. The preview shows one loop of a pattern, or the whole shape: drag its points to change it by hand, and every loop on the curve follows (Back to formula forgets it). Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y undo and redo your changes inside the window (Cancel still puts everything back). When its two halves match (like Wave, Bounce, S-curve or Circle), the points come as symmetric halves: moving a point moves its partner in the other half too. Double-click the line to add a point, right-click a point to remove it, Alt+drag for a sharp corner. The grid shows the numbers (x from 0 to 1 along one loop; y in keys); the mouse wheel zooms, dragging empty space (or middle-dragging) moves around, and Fit view shows all of it again. Save puts it in your list (patterns.json next to Spiderweb), and from then on it's in the Formula menu too.

Your own formula: tick Edit formula. A pattern is y of x for one loop (x goes from 0 to 1, y = how far to the side); a shape is x(t) and y(t), t going from 0 to 1 while it's drawn. Any other name in it (like height) gets its own number box. Works: numbers, + - * / ^ ( ), pi, e, sin cos tan asin acos atan sqrt exp ln log abs min max floor.

Remove formula takes them off (the curve you drew is left). Turn into plain curve makes what you see into ordinary anchors and handles (a line or an arc becomes a curve); if its two halves match, it gets Symmetric halves.

In the drawer, a pattern's sizes are hundredths of the board, so they grow and shrink with the placed shape. Funnel curves: a shape runs from the curve's start to its wall end inside the funnel (Slow start is x²); linked curves get the same formula; Back to the default curve resets it. Curve formulas saved in older versions (curves.json) are in the Shape list now.
The velocity pane has a Formula tool too: a line with a pattern swinging around it (see Velocity pane).

help.undo.title: Undo and redo
help.undo.tip: Made a mistake? Ctrl+Z = undo, Ctrl+Y = redo. Tick History in the toolbar to see every change as a step and jump back to any of them.
help.undo.text: Ctrl+Z undoes the last change, Ctrl+Y does it again. Ctrl+Z while something is half drawn drops just that.
Every change is a step with a name (the last 300 are kept). Tick History in the toolbar to see them all and click any step to jump straight to it (see History).
The drawer has its own Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y for its drawing.
help.undo.words: undo redo ctrl+z ctrl+y mistake back
help.history.title: History (undo steps)
help.history.tip: Every change is a step in the History list (tick History in the toolbar: it shows between Project and Shapes). Click a step to go back to it; Undock puts the list in a window of its own.
help.history.text: The History list (tick History in the toolbar; it shows in the side panel, between Project and Shapes) shows every change as a step, the oldest at the top: Start is how things were before the oldest step still kept (the last 300 are kept). The highlighted step is where you are now.

Click a step to go back to it: everything after it is undone and turns grey. Click a grey step to go forward again. Making a new change while steps are grey drops them (like Ctrl+Z and then changing something). Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y move up and down the same list. Typing in one box, or dragging a number box, is one step.
Undock puts the list in a window of its own that you can make taller; Dock (or closing that window) puts it back. Spiderweb remembers which, and where the window was.

help.selecting.title: Selecting, copying, flipping, turning
help.selecting.tip: Ctrl+click = more shapes, Ctrl+A = all. Ctrl+C / V = copy / paste at the play line. Ctrl+H / J = flip, Ctrl+Left / Right = turn 90°.
help.selecting.text: Ctrl+click selects more shapes (also in the Shapes list), Ctrl+A selects all.
Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V: copy / paste at the play line (snapped to the grid). Ctrl+D: duplicate. Del: delete.
Ctrl+H / Ctrl+J: flip sideways / upside down (sideways also mirrors velocities).
Ctrl+Left / Ctrl+Right: turn 90° as it looks on screen (the zoom decides how many beats a key becomes).
Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y: undo / redo. While something is half drawn, Ctrl+Z just drops that.
Settings in the panel (velocity, last note...) change every selected shape.

help.numbers.title: Number boxes
help.numbers.tip: Drag a box's name sideways to change it, or press Up / Down in the box. Shift = big steps, Ctrl = small steps.
help.numbers.text: Every number box can be changed without typing: drag the name next to it sideways, or press Up / Down in it (the mouse wheel too, while you're typing in it). Shift = big steps, Ctrl = small steps. A name over two boxes (Velocity, Gate) changes both. Boxes also take math: 960*4, 1920/3...

help.view.title: Scrolling and zooming
help.view.tip: Wheel = scroll, Shift+wheel = sideways, middle-drag = scroll. Ctrl+wheel = zoom (Ctrl+Shift = time only, Alt = keys only). Fit view (top) = see everything.
help.view.text: Wheel = scroll up / down, Shift+wheel = sideways. Ctrl+wheel = zoom both ways, Ctrl+Shift+wheel = zoom time, Alt+wheel = zoom pitch. Middle-drag, or dragging empty space with Select, scrolls. Fit view shows everything. The zoom and scroll are remembered.
Show lines / Show notes (top) hide the drawn lines or the notes. Keys outside a real 88-key piano are greyed on the keyboard.

Snap (top): the grid that points, moves and pastes snap to (Shift = free). Off, Bar, or a note length: a dot after the note = dotted (3/8 = a dotted quarter), a 3 = triplets (1/6 = quarter-note triplets). Custom… opens Customised snap: a number of notes (3 / 16 = three 16th notes), a dotted (.) or double-dotted (..) note, divided by a number (3 = triplets); it shows how long that is in beats and ticks.
help.view.words: zoom scroll pan fit view snap grid quantize quantise triplet dotted custom
help.velocity.title: Velocity pane
help.velocity.tip: Draw velocities over the bars: Linear, Curve, Pencil or Formula. With a shape selected only its notes change.
help.velocity.text: The pane under the piano roll shows every note's velocity. Draw over the bars with Linear, Curve, Pencil or Formula. With a shape selected, only its notes change (the others fade); with nothing selected, every note under the drag.

Formula: drag it like Linear; a pattern (Wave, Zigzag, Bounce or one you saved) swings the velocity up and down around the line. Pick the pattern, its Loops and height (in velocity steps) next to the tool buttons: changing them changes the line you just drew, until Enter or a click elsewhere.

Linear / Curve: drag it, then drag its end squares to move the ends (Ctrl = level with the other end) or a curve's round handle to bend it. Ctrl while drawing = flat. Hold Shift to snap the ends to the grid and, with a shape selected, onto its first / last note. Enter or a click outside the pane = done.
The velocities move and stretch with the shape. Typing a start / end velocity in the panel goes back to a straight ramp. Drag the bar above the pane to resize it; Velocity pane (top) hides it.
help.playback.title: Playing and listening
help.playback.tip: Space = play / stop. Right-drag = listen to the notes under the mouse.
help.playback.text: Space (or Play) plays from the play line through the MIDI out picked under Project; the blue line follows and the view turns the page. Click or drag the bar numbers (or click empty space with Select) to move the play line. Playing stops a moment after the last note.
Right-drag (any tool) = listen to the notes under the mouse, like scrubbing.
help.playback.words: play sound listen midi out scrub audio
help.channels.title: Channels
help.channels.tip: As drawn = everything kept. Single = one channel, overlaps fixed. Multi = overlapping shapes on different channels (each its own track).
help.channels.text: As drawn: every note exactly as the shapes make it, one channel; notes on the same key may overlap.

Single channel: where two notes on the same key overlap, the earlier one is cut where the later starts and the later one is stretched to where the earlier would have ended; notes starting on the same tick become one (the loudest, as long as the longest).

Multi channel: shapes whose notes clash go on different channels, each on its own track (channel 10, drums, is skipped). Split: Same key = only notes on the same key at the same time clash; Any notes = any notes at the same time. Shapes that follow one after another share a channel. Pasted notes (by track), live shapes made with Turn into live shape (by the shape each stroke came from) and Fill / Spam set to Outline (the outline and the inside) can spread over several channels: the shape list says how many, in orange above 15 (from there the colours and channel numbers repeat).
Every channel has its own note colour.
help.files.title: Saving and MIDI export
help.files.tip: Your work saves itself. Generate MIDI writes the .mid file set under Project.
help.files.text: Everything is saved on its own (autosave.json next to Spiderweb) and comes back next time; each time Spiderweb starts, the previous session is kept as autosave-backup.json. Save… / Open… keep and open project files (.json). Shapes are stored in beats, so changing PPQ doesn't move them.
Generate MIDI writes the file set under Output file, with the PPQ, BPM and beats per bar from Project. PPQ 32767 or higher: many MIDI programs can't open the file (the box turns red).

Keys (under Project) set to 256: the piano roll goes up to key 255 instead of 127, and the MIDI file keeps those keys. That's for players that support 256 keys (handy for tunings like 31edo, which need more keys per octave). Many MIDI programs can't read keys above 127, and playback here skips them. Back at 128, notes above 127 are left out; the shapes stay as they are.
If something goes wrong, the details go to errors.log next to Spiderweb.

help.domino.title: Copy to / Paste from Domino
help.domino.tip: Ctrl+Shift+C copies the notes; paste them in Domino with Ctrl+V. Ctrl+Shift+V pastes notes copied in Domino as one shape.
help.domino.text: Copy to Domino (under Project, or Ctrl+Shift+C) puts the selected shapes' notes on the clipboard, or all notes when nothing is selected. In Domino, pick the track and press Ctrl+V, or double-click where the notes should go.
The dropdown above the buttons sets where the notes start, for copying and pasting both:
• First note at tick 0: the first note lands right on Domino's cursor (or on the play line here).
• From the bar line: the empty space from the bar line before the first note comes along, so paste on a bar line and the notes keep their place in the bar.
As drawn / Single channel: everything goes into the track you paste into, on that track's channel.

Multi channel: each channel with notes becomes a track, in channel order, packed together (channels without notes are skipped): the first goes into the track you paste into, the next into the track below it, and so on. The pasted notes play on those tracks' own channels, and tracks that don't fit below the last one are dropped.

Ticks are copied as they are: with a different PPQ in Domino the notes come out longer or shorter, so set the same PPQ in both (or use that on purpose). With 256 keys, notes above key 127 are left out (Domino has 128 keys).

Paste from Domino (or Ctrl+Shift+V) works the other way: select notes in Domino, press Ctrl+C there, then paste here. The start of what you copied (or its first note, see the dropdown) lands on the play line (snapped to the grid), like pasting in Domino, and ticks are taken as they are. The notes of every copied track become ONE shape (Pasted notes); controllers and other events are left out. Each note remembers its track: with Multi channel every track counts as a shape of its own (tracks that overlap get different channels, the others can share one), with Single channel all of them go on one channel and overlaps are removed. If Ctrl+Shift+V does nothing, another program (often a clipboard manager) has taken that shortcut for itself: free it in that program's settings, or use the button.

Move, flip, turn, stretch or skew the shape like a custom shape: the notes go with its box. The notes keep their own velocities until you change the shape's velocity (in the panel or the velocity pane).

help.drawer.title: The drawer
help.drawer.tip: Draw a shape for your library, Save it, then Use on the piano roll. Closed outlines can be filled.
help.drawer.text: The drawer (Custom shape → Drawer…) is where you draw shapes for your library. Its tools work like the piano roll's: Line, Polyline, Freehand, Curve (C), Arc, Square, Circle (O), Eraser, and Select. Points snap to the grid; Shift draws freely. Drag a stroke out, or click where it starts and click where it ends (right-click or Esc cancels).
Save keeps it in the library (the shapes subfolder next to Spiderweb); Use on the piano roll picks it for the Custom shape tool. On the piano roll it stretches to the box you drag.

Lines and curves that meet end to end count as one outline. Closed: Empty, Fill and Spam all work. Gaps (red dots at the loose ends): Fill and Spam close each one with a straight line (see Inside fill).
Wheel = zoom, middle-drag = scroll, Reset view = back to the middle of the board.
help.drawer_select.title: Drawer: Select and editing
help.drawer_select.tip: Drag a point (small squares), a stroke, or empty space to scroll. Del = delete the stroke.
help.drawer_select.text: Select: drag a point (small squares; points in the same spot move together, so outlines stay closed), an ellipse's corners, or a whole stroke (moves in grid squares, Shift = free). Drag empty space to scroll. Del deletes the selected stroke.
Right-click a stroke = its menu (add point / anchor, symmetric curve halves, delete, copy, paste, flip, turn); empty space = deselect; while drawing a polyline = finish it.

Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V = copy / paste (each paste lands one more grid square down and right), Ctrl+H / Ctrl+J = flip sideways / upside down, Ctrl+Left / Ctrl+Right = turn 90°. These work on the selected stroke, or the whole drawing when nothing is selected.
help.drawer_select.words: drawer edit move copy flip turn
help.drawer_line.title: Drawer: Line
help.drawer_line.tip: Drag from start to end, or click both.
help.drawer_line.text: Drag from start to end, or click the start and click the end.
help.drawer_poly.title: Drawer: Polyline
help.drawer_poly.tip: Click points (or drag each piece). Click the first point again to close it.
help.drawer_poly.text: Click points, or drag each piece. Click the first point again to close it; double-click or right-click stops.
help.drawer_free.title: Drawer: Freehand
help.drawer_free.tip: Drag to draw. Let go near the start to close it.
help.drawer_free.text: Hold the mouse button and draw. Letting go near the start closes it.
help.drawer_curve.title: Drawer: Curve
help.drawer_curve.tip: From start to end, then bend it with its blue handles. Middle-click it = new anchor.
help.drawer_curve.text: Drag (or click) from start to end. The new curve is selected: bend it with its handles like any curve (see Curves: anchors and handles); middle-click near it adds an anchor. Right-click it: Formula (a shape or a pattern along it, see Formulas).
help.drawer_arc.title: Drawer: Arc
help.drawer_arc.tip: Click start, a point it passes through, end. Or drag start to end, then click to bend.
help.drawer_arc.text: Click its start, a point it passes through, then its end (or drag from start to end, then click to set the bend): a piece of a perfect circle. End on the start = a whole circle. Select: drag its three points.
help.drawer_square.title: Drawer: Square
help.drawer_square.tip: Corner to corner. Ctrl = a perfect square.
help.drawer_square.text: Drag (or click) corner to corner; Ctrl makes it a perfect square.
help.drawer_circle.title: Drawer: Circle
help.drawer_circle.tip: Corner to corner. Ctrl = a perfect circle.
help.drawer_circle.text: Drag (or click) corner to corner of its box; Ctrl makes it a perfect circle.
help.drawer_erase.title: Drawer: Eraser
help.drawer_erase.tip: Click a stroke to remove it. Ctrl+Z = undo.
help.drawer_erase.text: Click a stroke to remove it. Ctrl+Z = undo.
help.shortcuts.title: Keyboard and mouse shortcuts
help.shortcuts.tip: Every key and mouse shortcut in one list.
help.shortcuts.text: Tools: V Select, L Line, P Polyline, F Freehand, C Curve, A Arc, S Custom shape, Q Square, O Circle, T Triangle, N Funnel, X Text. G = Live shape on / off.
Drawing: Shift = don't snap. Ctrl = perfect (square, circle, triangle, proportions). Right-click or Esc = cancel what's half drawn. Enter / double-click = finish a polyline.

Mouse: right-click a shape = its menu, empty space = deselect. Double right-click = Select ↔ last tool. Right-drag = listen. Middle-click = add a point / anchor / funnel curve start. Middle-drag = scroll.
Wheel = scroll, Shift+wheel = sideways, Ctrl+wheel = zoom, Ctrl+Shift+wheel = zoom time, Alt+wheel = zoom pitch.

Editing: Del delete, Ctrl+D duplicate, Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y undo / redo (see History), Ctrl+A select all, Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V copy / paste, Ctrl+H / Ctrl+J flip, Ctrl+Left / Ctrl+Right turn 90°, Ctrl+G join into one curve, Ctrl+Shift+G split into separate shapes, Ctrl+L turn into live shape, Ctrl+K claw machine, Esc clear highlight / unpick a stroke. With a stroke of a live shape picked, the copy / paste / flip / turn keys work on that stroke.
Playing: Space play / stop. Click or drag the bar numbers = move the play line.
Curves: Alt+drag a handle = sharp corner, Alt+drag an anchor = new handles, Ctrl = change only this curve (linked funnel curves).
Number boxes: drag the name, Up / Down, wheel; Shift = big steps, Ctrl = small.
F1 = Help. Ctrl+S = save. Ctrl+Shift+C = Copy to Domino, Ctrl+Shift+V = Paste from Domino.
claw.n_shapes: {n} shapes (they all get the same settings)
claw.tip_mode:
How the notes are picked:
By time: cuts slices of time out, like the claw machine of other piano rolls.
Count notes / keys / chords: keep some, trash some, over and over (notes starting together = one chord).
Random: keeps notes picked at random.
claw.tip_keep: How many to keep before trashing some.
claw.tip_skip: How many to throw away after the ones kept. 0 = keep everything.
claw.tip_pct: About this many notes in every hundred stay; which ones is random.
claw.tip_new_random: Pick other notes at random (the same number of them).
claw.tip_shorten: The notes picked to go stay, only shorter.
claw.tip_cut: How long they stay: this much of their length (at least 1 tick).
claw.tip_period: The claw works on this much time at a time, over and over, starting at the shape's first note.
claw.tip_trash:
Cuts each period into equal slices and throws one away: 1/4 = the first quarter, 2/4 = the second quarter, and so on.
Notes in it go, notes crossing its edges are cut, and the later notes move earlier to close the gap.
claw.tip_dist:
Bends time inside each period.
Right: long notes first, then faster and faster. Left: the other way round.
Drag up / down (Shift = fine), mouse wheel or arrow keys; it stops at 0 for a moment on the way past.
Right mouse button: points it at the mouse. Middle-click (press the wheel) = back to 0.
claw.tip_stretch: Stretches the result back to the shape's full length (the notes get longer too).
claw.tip_short: Removes notes the claw left very short (under 1/24 beat). Notes that were that short already stay.
claw.tip_reset: Everything back to the start (the claw then changes nothing).
